sample_unit: GPT-4 generated simplified CMR reports (from 20 original reports)

links.outcome: Readability (ARI) and layperson understandability of GPT-4 simplified reports vs original reports
links.effect: ARI 10 [9-12] original vs 5 [4-6] GPT-4 (p<0.001); 2/60 (3%) GPT-4 reports vs 18/20 (90%) originals at 8th grade level or higher; laypersons rated GPT-4 easier to understand (1 vs 4, p<0.001).
links.quote: Eighteen out of 20 (90%) standard CMR reports and 2/60 (3%) GPT-generated reports had an ARI score corresponding to the 8th grade level or higher.

links.outcome: Factual correctness, completeness, and lack of harm of GPT-4 report explanations rated by radiologists
links.effect: Ratings median 5 for correctness, completeness, and lack of harm; strong agreement for factual correctness in 94% (113/120) and completeness in 81% (97/120) of ratings. Not tested specifically in low-literacy users.
links.quote: Radiologists' ratings of the GPT-4 reports reached high levels for correctness (5 [4, 5]), completeness (5 [5]), and lack of potential harm (5 [5]); with "strong agreement" for factual correctness in 94% (113/120) and completeness of relevant findings in 81% (97/120) of reports.

links.outcome: Reproducibility of layperson understandability across three GPT-4 outputs from same report
links.effect: Test-retest agreement for layperson understandability ratings across three simplified reports was substantial (ICC 0.62; p<0.001).
links.quote: Test-retest agreement for layperson understandability ratings between the three simplified reports generated from the same original report was substantial (ICC: 0.62; p < 0.001).

screen.reason: Evaluates GPT-4 for simplifying cardiovascular magnetic resonance reports for laypersons using expert and layperson ratings, without testing an organizational safeguard or deployment intervention.
